name: The Age of Adventurers
description: The age in which expeditions and champions repeatedly crossed the world's thresholds: Ahn'Qiraj, Outland, Northrend, the Cataclysm, Pandaria, alternate Draenor, the Broken Isles, and Argus.

name: Rise of the Ancient Civilizations
description: The first troll powers, the war with the aqir, the rise and fall of the mogu empire, and the ascent of the kaldorei around the Well of Eternity.

name: Primordial Azeroth and the Black Empire
description: Azeroth's immense nascent world-soul left its native elementals without enough Spirit to balance them. Their long conflict was overtaken by the arrival of the Old Gods and the civilization their servants raised across the primordial world.

name: Cosmic Origins
description: The cited account begins with Light and Shadow, the birth of the physical universe and Twisting Nether, the awakening of world-souls, the gathering of the titan Pantheon, and the Void Lords' attempt to corrupt a nascent titan through the Old Gods.

name: The Long Vigil and the New Kingdoms
description: The kaldorei begin the Long Vigil while migrations, alliances, wars, and political fragmentation establish Quel'Thalas, Arathor's successor kingdoms, and the divided powers of Khaz Modan.

name: The Modern Cosmic Age
description: A wounded world passes through the Fourth War, N’Zoth, the Shadowlands, the Dragon Isles, Khaz Algar, shattered K’aresh, and the released Midnight crisis in Quel’Thalas. Later Worldsoul Saga outcomes remain open.

name: Ordering of Azeroth
description: The Pantheon intervenes to save Azeroth, the keeper-led titan-forged break the Black Empire, the surviving Old Gods are imprisoned, and the wounded world is stabilized and reshaped.

name: The Rise of the Horde and the First Two Wars
description: Draenor's corruption, the orcs' fall to the Legion, opening of the Dark Portal, destruction of Stormwind, and the Alliance victory in the Second War.

name: The Third War and the Frozen Throne
description: The Scourge, Arthas's downfall, destruction of Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas, the Legion's return, the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and the creation of the Lich King's new order.

name: The War of the Ancients and the Sundering
description: Political choices around the Well enabled the Burning Legion's first invasion, drew defenders from across ancient Kalimdor, and ended with the Great Sundering.

description: Ysida Harmon, represented in the Dungeon Set 2 research story.

name: Zin-Azshari
description: Azshara's capital at the shores of the Well of Eternity and the center of the Highborne portal ritual.

name: Ancient Zuldazar
description: The highland center of the Zandalar tribe and a political heart of the earliest troll civilization represented in this era.

name: The War Effort Opens Ahn'Qiraj
description: Alliance and Horde communities supplied a shared war effort before champions entered Ahn'Qiraj to confront C'Thun's forces.

name: The Alliance of Lordaeron Forms
description: Stormwind's warning and the approaching Horde threat drew human kingdoms and allied peoples into a military coalition centered on Lordaeron.

name: The Allied Powers Defeat the Amani
description: The combined high-elven and human campaign broke the immediate Amani offensive and sharply reduced the empire's regional power without ending the Amani people.

name: Awakening of Aman’Thul
description: Aman’Thul awoke from the world that had nurtured his spirit and began searching the cosmos for other nascent titans.

name: The Aqir Awaken
description: Ancient aqir forces emerged again and pressed into troll-held lands, turning scattered rivalry into a shared existential danger.

name: The Aqir Successor Powers Emerge
description: Separated aqir populations entrenched themselves in distant refuges, producing new northern and southern powers rather than restoring one united dominion.

name: Arathor Fragments into the Seven Kingdoms
description: Over generations, Arathor's distant city-states became sovereign powers and the unified human empire gave way to seven kingdoms.

name: Archimonde Is Destroyed at Mount Hyjal
description: The defenders delayed Archimonde until Malfurion released Nordrassil's gathered power, destroying the Legion commander and repelling the assault.

name: Archimonde Is Summoned into Azeroth
description: The Scourge's campaign opened the way for Archimonde and the Burning Legion to return and turn their advance toward Kalimdor and Nordrassil.

name: The Campaign Reaches Argus
description: A direct link carried the coalition to shattered Argus and the Burning Legion's seat of power.

name: Arthas Ascends the Frozen Throne
description: After defeating Illidan, Arthas reached the Frozen Throne and joined with the Lich King, establishing the new order that closes this era.

name: Arthas Claims Frostmourne
description: Arthas pursued the Scourge into Northrend and took up Frostmourne, a choice that bound his fate more tightly to the Lich King.

name: Azeroth Is Ordered
description: The titan-forged raised mountains, opened waterways, dredged seas, maintained great works, and helped make the wounded world stable enough for life to flourish.

name: Azshara Rises to the Throne
description: Azshara became queen of a powerful kaldorei civilization whose court and arcane ambitions stood at the threshold of the next catastrophe.

name: Black Empire Dominion
description: The elementals failed to dislodge the Old Gods and were enslaved; without that resistance, Black Empire influence extended over much of the world.

name: Rise of the Black Empire
description: The n'raqi directed the aqir in building citadels and temple cities around the Old Gods; Y'Shaarj's central bastion became the greatest of these domains as their holdings spread.

name: The Legion's Crusade Is Broken
description: The Argus campaign broke the Burning Legion's immediate cosmic crusade, closing the era with victory and a wounded world left behind.

name: The Class Orders Rise Against the Legion
description: As the Burning Legion invaded through the Broken Isles, distinct class orders organized champions for a common defense.

name: The Curse of Ula’tek Reaches the Coiled Isle
description: The Midnight campaign continues on the Coiled Isle as Zul’jarra pursues Zul’jan and champions confront the Ula’tek threat.

name: The Dark Portal Opens
description: Gul'dan and the corrupted Guardian Medivh completed a gateway between Draenor and Azeroth, allowing the Horde to cross between worlds.

name: The Dark Trolls Settle Near the Well
description: A reclusive dark troll people moved toward the center of Kalimdor and made their home near the Well of Eternity.

name: The Elven Coalition Creates the Dawnwell
description: An elven coalition drives back the Devouring Host, Sylvanas helps force Xal’atath to retreat, and the corrupted fount becomes the Dawnwell.

name: Deathwing Shatters the World
description: Deathwing's return caused the Cataclysm, violently reshaping regions across Azeroth and forcing a world-spanning defense.

name: The Dragon Isles Awaken
description: The Dragon Isles awakened, calling the dragonflights home and opening a new expedition into their ancient inheritance.

name: A commission from Booty Bay
description: Bodley remembers a commission from Gremnik Rizzlesprang, a goblin smuggler-wizard out of Booty Bay. The job was to take Lord Valthalak’s spellbook from Blackrock Spire. Bodley does not know whether Gremnik meant to study it or sell it, and the manual leaves that motive unresolved. The distinction matters: the company’s contract is documented, but its patron’s private purpose is not.

name: A plea that cannot wait
description: Anthion’s request carries two losses at once. He has already died in the attempt, yet the thought of losing Ysida still binds him to the road. The quest asks for a living woman held by the Baron, not for a heroic last stand by her husband. No timer is needed in the telling: the source gives the plea and the danger, while the hourglass belongs to the dungeon challenge rather than to a new historical event.

name: Alternative fate · Isalien
description: Isalien left the company for a pilgrimage to Dire Maul, seeking answers about her night elf heritage and perhaps the magic within her amulet piece. Bodley remembers her as a friend of Falrin. In the city’s old kaldorei halls, she was ambushed by Alzzin the Wildshaper and his forces. The manual leaves her at another haunted place: a former companion drawn toward knowledge, then overtaken by the same scattered curse.

name: Alternative fate · Jarien and Sothos
description: Jarien and Sothos, siblings of the Veiled Blade, turned toward the Scarlet Crusade after the company dissolved. They sought knighthood at Stratholme. Bodley’s account says Sothos failed the final trial; Jarien defended her brother and demanded that they be admitted together. Grand Crusader Dathrohan killed them both. The amulet piece they carried further twisted their spirits. Their chapter, too, is one possible haunted locus in the family of routes.

name: Alternative fate · Kormok
description: Another branch follows Kormok to Scholomance. Once a member of the Veiled Blade, the two-headed ogre became drawn to necromancy; the manual describes one head as clever and cold, the other more foolish. After the company broke apart, he sought further study at Scholomance. Valthalak’s spectral assassins reached him there and killed him before Ras Frostwhisper. The record remembers a comrade turned toward dangerous art, then found by the curse.

name: Alternative fate · Mor Grayhoof
description: One remembered branch leads to Mor Grayhoof. He survived the fall into Lower Blackrock Spire, but trolls captured him and War Master Voone tortured him. The spectral assassins finished what the fall had not. Mor’s story is one of the manual’s haunted loci; it is an alternative account of a former companion’s fate, not an assertion that every adventurer fought every spirit in this order.

name: Bodley, unseen on the balcony
description: Near the entrance balcony of Blackrock Spire, Bodley appears only to one who can see ghosts. He had gone back toward the fortress and never returned. The quest giver fears he is dead; Bodley confirms it without ceremony and asks for help undoing the company’s wrong. If the top piece is already found, he can point toward the other two. His greeting is warm, even here, where the old danger began.

name: Falrin remembers an old friend
description: In Dire Maul’s Athenaeum, Anthion’s old friend Falrin Treeshaper listens to the request. He had thought Anthion dead. Falrin agrees to help prepare an enchantment that can draw Theldren into a fight; his anger at the ogres is personal, rooted in the death of his brother. The required collection is a task in play, not a separate historical episode. What matters to the story is that an old bond supplies the means for a dangerous meeting.

name: Ysida in the Slaughter House
description: The way leads through Stratholme to its Slaughter House, where Rivendare holds Ysida. The walls are steeped in the Scourge’s greenish corruption, but the quest’s purpose is rescue: reach her alive and bring her beyond the Baron’s reach. The art marks the room as an interpretation of the Classic dungeon, not a measured reconstruction. Ysida has endured the city’s horror; the next journey carries a message toward the husband she believes is lost.

name: Mea Culpa, Lord Valthalak
description: In the Beast’s chamber, the brazier calls Valthalak back into a body that can be confronted. After the battle, the restored amulet is used on his corpse and his spirit appears, whole again. He recognizes that the seeker was not among the original thieves and demands his property back. The quest does not give the mortal a new claim to the medallion; it asks the traveler to return it to its owner and carry his answer back to Bodley.

name: Anthion’s parting words
description: With the top piece returned, Anthion explains the danger that he could not see before. The Veiled Blade split Valthalak’s amulet into three parts out of greed, not knowing that it held much of the warlock’s soul. The curse followed. Anthion asks the seeker to find Bodley, who can guide the search for the other pieces. At last, Anthion believes he may rest; his part in the company’s wrong has become a plea to set it right.

name: Proof of life
description: Ysida gives the rescuer her locket to carry back to Anthion. She believes he perished while trying to save her, and the token is her proof that she remains alive. When the message reaches the roadside ghost, Anthion learns that the rescue succeeded. Their reunion is brief and divided by death, yet Ysida’s survival releases him from the fear that held him there. He can now offer help in the work that remains.

name: Safe for now
description: Valthalak tells the traveler to return to the Veiled Blade and say they are safe—for now. Bodley is astonished that the spirit will call off his assassins, though the promise carries a warning of future harm. The manual still speaks of echoes at the haunted loci, and the company itself has not been restored. Its members remain scattered among separate lives and deaths. What is repaired is the amulet, and for this moment, the pursuit it unleashed.

name: The brazier is prepared
description: Bodley prepares a brazier able to call the spirit from its old lair. The chain asks for specific components, but their collection is not another history of the company. Its purpose is to attune the brazier and make the final encounter possible. The manual names haunted places to give the wider meaning: Valthalak’s power has marked the places where his former companions fell, and the Beast’s chamber remains the last of those sites.

name: The company flees the risen spirit
description: Valthalak rose as a spirit and called spectral assassins against the mercenaries. Their struggle also roused defenders in the Spire. Most of the Veiled Blade escaped, but safety proved brief: the assassins pursued them wherever they hid. The company soon broke apart, its quarrel made worse by a curse that followed each shard. In the confusion Mor Grayhoof fell toward the lower reaches of the fortress, where his own path would end.

name: A fragment taken by Theldren
description: Anthion’s next account turns from rescue to the Veiled Blade’s spoils. The company did not understand the medallion’s importance, so it was divided with their other plunder. A dwarf named Theldren took the first piece. Anthion tried to win it back and was beaten badly; the fragment would have to be claimed through another challenge. The amulet is already more than an ornament, though its danger has not yet been named.

name: The former general of the Spire
description: Before Drakkisath, Lord Valthalak was a drakonid noble and warlock who had served as Blackrock Spire’s general. The Veiled Blade entered the upper fortress, slew him, and took the spellbook. Bodley recalls that the company knew too little of Valthalak’s power over souls to understand what they had disturbed. The lair is now called the Beast’s chamber. The manual’s account makes clear that the company’s successful contract was the beginning of its ruin.

name: The ghost at Stratholme’s gate
description: At the Eastern Plaguelands road, a goblin device lets the living hear Anthion Harmon. Death has not quieted his concern: Ysida, his wife, was captured by Baron Rivendare inside Stratholme. Anthion says he tried to reach her and failed. He asks the seeker to finish the rescue. The city rises behind him through bare branches and grey-green haze; within it, the question is simple and terrible—whether Ysida still lives.

name: The medallion in Kormok’s hands
description: When the company prepared to leave with the book, Kormok claimed Valthalak’s amulet as his share. His insistence turned the group against itself. They argued, nearly came to blows, and finally broke the medallion into three pieces. Only later did they learn that it housed much of Valthalak’s spirit. The distribution followed a lot; Theldren’s top fragment had already returned through Anthion’s challenge, while the other pieces scattered among former companions.

name: Finding the other two pieces
description: Bodley guides the search to two further pieces. The quest versions can direct a class or faction branch toward one of several haunted companions; they are alternate targets from the same company history. The four accounts just heard are arranged here as memorials, not as four mandatory kills by one canonical traveler. When the missing pieces are brought together with Theldren’s top fragment, the medallion can be made whole again.

name: The Challenge in Blackrock Depths
description: Beneath Blackrock Mountain, the Ring of Law becomes the stage for the challenge. As High Justice Grimstone sentences the intruders, they plant Falrin’s banner. Theldren cannot resist the provocation; he enters the arena with his gladiators. The team composition can vary, so this scene gives no fixed roster or race to the company. The battle retrieves the top piece and changes the next question: now the remaining fragments must be traced to Anthion’s other companions.

name: Two doors into the same story
description: Deliana speaks from Ironforge; Mokvar speaks from Orgrimmar. Their faction quests are separate doors into the same old wound, not a shared meeting or a single adventurer’s simultaneous allegiance. Each directs a seeker toward Anthion Harmon, whose ghost waits beyond Stratholme. The armor work that frames the journey is only its threshold. Ahead lie a rescue, a company’s last contract, and a medallion whose pieces carried more than any of its owners understood.

name: The Dwarven Succession Crisis Opens
description: The death of Ironforge's high king broke a tense balance among the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans and opened a war for the mountain city.

name: The Early Troll Powers Rise
description: Troll peoples flourished across the forests and jungles of ordered Kalimdor, with the Zandalar, Amani, Gurubashi, and Drakkari among the powers that took shape.

name: Azsharite for the weapon
description: A name alone cannot break Razelikh’s hold. The chain next calls for azsharite, a material gathered in Azshara and brought into the weapon-making task. The quest’s collection condition is not retold as a count or a single dramatic excavation. What changes is the preparation: the hunt has found its target, and the seeker now carries material chosen for the Felbane armament that will make the final confrontation possible.

name: Bengor brings the lost orders
description: In the Horde telling, Bengor is found wounded in the Swamp of Sorrows. He reports that the dispatch was ambushed and the Warchief’s orders lost. His testimony brings the seeker to Trebor and gives the campaign a practical beginning: before the old soldier can speak of his shame, the missing command must be recovered. The chain does not turn the Alliance introduction into the same journey; it offers another way to reach the shared wound.

name: Felbane takes shape
description: At Galvan’s camp in inland Stranglethorn, the material becomes Felbane weaponry. The green canopy, hanging vines and warm air make the setting recognizably different from Azshara’s coast; this is no harbor scene at Booty Bay. Galvan’s part is the transformation of gathered material into a prepared weapon. The records support the chain’s order and purpose, while the exact craft process and selectable weapon form remain matters for comparison with the Classic client.

name: A sign of hope, and an unfinished charge
description: The final quest records Razelikh’s defeat and asks that his horn be returned to Trebor as a sign of hope. It also asks for the Ward of the Defiler so Trebor can destroy it. The request is clear; the destruction itself is not shown as a completed event in the evidence used here. Trebor’s story reaches a hard-won answer for the bound souls and the demon who held them. It does not record the fall of the Burning Legion, or every fate within its reach.

name: Kirith at Serpent’s Coil
description: The quest turns toward Serpent’s Coil, where Kirith the Damned bars the way. The setting changes from open badlands to a low cave mouth on the coast. There the adventurer defeats the demon and the chain yields a new account through Kirith’s spirit. The art presents the beast in a broad, readable silhouette; it is not a reconstruction of the cave’s exact layout or proof of details absent from the quest record.

name: The amulet has three pieces
description: Kirith’s spirit explains the next obstacle: Razelikh cannot be reached until the shattered amulet is made whole. Its three pieces are held by the demon’s lieutenants. The quest dialogue supplies the clue, not a new claim about Kirith’s final fate. The fragments now give the scattered work a shape. Trebor’s grievance can be answered only by confronting the power behind the bindings, and the seeker needs both knowledge and a weapon for that meeting.

name: Loramus and the demon hunter’s counsel
description: The chain reaches Loramus Thalipedes on Azshara’s cold eastern shore. In the Classic quest account, the demon hunter helps direct the work that lies ahead: learn the demon’s true name and prepare a means to challenge him. The coast is broad and wind-cut, a different world from the Blasted Lands’ dry scar. This telling uses Loramus’s Classic-era counsel only; later retellings of his story do not replace what this quest chain records.

name: The name behind the title
description: The search crosses Azshara’s pale coastal ruins, where the quest steps call for Hetaera’s blood and seek Lord Arkkoroc’s knowledge. The demon known as Razelikh the Defiler bears a truer name: Rakh’likh. That distinction is the chain’s discovery. Here, the old temple stone and blue water frame a hunt for usable knowledge, not a claim that every step took place in one room or followed an exact route along the coast.

name: Return with the forged weapons
description: The quest line turns back to Trebor with the weapon prepared and the amulet’s scattered fragments to unite. This is an editorial journey through quest destinations, not a drawn route: its tasks name the regions but do not document each road taken. The exposed Blasted Lands return as the place where old bonds and new preparations converge. The demon’s title, the weapon and the amulet are now part of one effort to reach the Rise.

name: The stones that bind them
description: The quest objective names eighteen bound servants: nine held by Razelikh and three each by Sevine, Allistarj and Grol. Their binding is represented by stones spread across the region, with no exact placement claimed here. The quest asks the seeker to break the hold upon them. In the exposed red earth, Trebor’s old loss becomes more than a memory: it becomes a task that can still release those who suffered under his command.

name: At the Rise of the Defiler
description: At the Rise of the Defiler, the united amulet lets the seeker bring the demon into the final contest. The known title falls away before the true name: Razelikh is Rakh’likh. Trebor’s old appeal has led here, from the souls once bound by the demon’s servants to a challenge against their master. The quests frame the meeting as a dangerous group confrontation but give no fixed battle formation. At the Rise, every preparation finds its purpose against the master whose servants once held Trebor’s soldiers.

name: The spirits may rest
description: When the binding stones are broken, the completion text says the tortured souls can rest. It gives Trebor the mercy he had sought for his soldiers, though the count remains unsettled by the separate nineteen-men line. The story pauses over that release without supplying names for the dead or turning each stone into a separate battle. A long burden has eased; the power behind the chains still stands.

name: Three lieutenants, three fragments
description: The remaining amulet pieces come from Razelikh’s lieutenants: Allistarj, Sevine and Grol. Their encounters are separate, not one gathering in a field. In the tour they form a deliberate triptych, a memorial arrangement of three independent confrontations. When the fragments are brought together, the amulet is whole. Its completion opens the way that Kirith described, though the precise order of lieutenant encounters is not treated as a historical sequence beyond the quest dependency.

name: Trebor’s tale of sorrow
description: Trebor recounts failure in battle, then a return to the Blasted Lands to rescue the men left behind. The account is one of defeat and obligation: he could not leave the captured soldiers to their torment. The reproduced Horde dialogue speaks of nineteen of his men, while the binding-stone objective counts eighteen bound servants. These are kept as two source details in tension. The surviving evidence does not resolve the difference.

name: Two roads to the Fallen Hero
description: The Blasted Lands are a country of exposed earth and old ruin, where Trebor’s defeat still has living consequences. Classic gives his story two introductions. The Alliance quest approaches him through a plea for common action against the Legion; the Horde chain follows lost orders and a courier’s report. These are separate faction paths, not one traveler’s shared itinerary. They meet at Trebor, whose concern has outlasted his own life: the soldiers he could not save.

name: The First War Begins
description: Horde forces entered Azeroth and began the war against the Kingdom of Stormwind.

name: The Forsaken Emerge in Lordaeron
description: Sylvanas and other undead broke from the Lich King's control and established a new, precarious power in the ruins of Lordaeron.

name: The Fourth War Campaign Ends
description: A rebellion joined with Alliance pressure against Sylvanas's rule, bringing the war campaign to its end without erasing its losses.

name: The Fourth War Erupts
description: Alliance and Horde entered a global war of footholds, reprisals, and deepening fractures after the Legion's defeat.

name: The Great Sundering
description: The Well's destruction tore primordial Kalimdor apart, drowned great reaches of land, and left the Maelstrom at the center of a new ocean.

name: Grom Breaks Mannoroth's Bond
description: After falling again beneath Mannoroth's corruption, Grom joined Thrall against the pit lord and died in the act that broke the immediate demonic bond over their people.

name: Gul'dan Abandons the Second War
description: Gul'dan withdrew forces from the Horde's campaign for his own expedition, weakening Orgrim's offensive at a critical time.

name: Gul'dan Forms the Shadow Council
description: After Ner'zhul resisted the Legion's course, Gul'dan organized a concealed warlock council and tightened hidden control around the forming Horde.

name: The Highborne Are Exiled
description: Conflict over arcane practice ended with a Highborne population leaving Kalimdor under Dath'Remar's leadership.

name: The Highborne Open the Way
description: Azshara's favored Highborne used the Well to establish a portal through which the Burning Legion could enter Azeroth.

name: The Horde Is Defeated and the Dark Portal Is Destroyed
description: The Alliance drove the Horde back to the gateway, destroyed the original Dark Portal, and captured many of the defeated orcs.

name: The Defenders of Hyjal Unite
description: Night elves, the New Horde, and Alliance survivors accepted a temporary common defense as the Legion advanced toward Mount Hyjal.

name: Illidan Assaults the Frozen Throne
description: Illidan returned from Outland and drove toward Icecrown, but Arthas defeated him before reaching the Frozen Throne.

name: Illidan Creates a Second Well
description: Illidan used preserved water from the original Well to create a new arcane well upon Mount Hyjal and was imprisoned after the act was discovered.

name: Illidan Seizes Power in Outland
description: Illidan and his allies closed portals, defeated Magtheridon's rule, and established a new center of power in Outland.

name: The Iron Horde Opens an Alternate Front
description: An invasion from an alternate Draenor opened a separate-world campaign against the Iron Horde.

name: The Kaldorei Ascend
description: Changed by long proximity to the Well, the emerging kaldorei mastered arcane power, built cities, and expanded across Kalimdor.

name: A key in three pieces
description: Khadgar explains that, while stranded in Outland, he split his key into three and hid the pieces inside enchanted containers. The places seemed safe when he chose them; Outland has changed since then. His explanation gives the search its shape, but not a single road: each fragment lies in a separate dungeon, and each location reflects a world now fought over by new powers.

name: Beneath the sealed tower
description: Alturus gives the seeker a Violet Scrying Crystal and asks for readings from underground water in the Master’s Cellar. In the quest’s report, the expected arcane currents are absent: the tower registers as a vast energy vacuum, with only a faint demonic echo. That phrase is Alturus’s reading of the crystal, not a confirmed identity for the presence. The cellar returns a warning, but not yet an answer.

name: A question among the ashes
description: After studying the journal, Alturus proposes that Medivh may have woven some of his essence into the magic that defeated Arcanagos. If so, he reasons, a trace might remain in the dragon’s bones. The quest sends the seeker to find a Charred Bone Fragment in the mountains south of Karazhan. This is Alturus’s hypothesis and a search for evidence, not a confirmation that the essence can be recovered.

name: A report reaches Dalaran
description: Alturus sends his report to Archmage Cedric in Dalaran’s old crater. Cedric has learned that the tower sealed itself off and that the Violet Eye lost contact with agents within it. The new reading gives the old silence another urgency. Cedric points toward one person who might reopen the way: Khadgar, Medivh’s former apprentice, now living in Shattrath. The ruined crater is Dalaran’s original site, not the city’s later home in Northrend.

name: The first fragment in Auchindoun
description: The first fragment rests in the Shadow Labyrinth, among passages occupied by the Shadow Council. Khadgar’s account places the container there because the labyrinth once seemed a safe hiding place. The return of the fragment changes the key from a distant memory into a recoverable object. It does not yet open the tower; two pieces remain beyond reach.

name: Kalynna’s offer
description: Alturus sends the bone to Kalynna Lathred in Area 52. She once belonged to the Kirin Tor, but now follows studies her old order forbade. The fragment’s essence, Alturus says, is lifeless—like Arcanagos. Kalynna believes she can help, but her own research has a cost. Her answer turns the Violet Eye’s question into a bargain between scholars with different boundaries.

name: Two books, two halls
description: Kalynna asks for two books before she will complete the favor. The Tome of Dusk belongs to the orc warlock Nethekurse in the Shattered Halls; the Book of Forgotten Names is held by Darkweaver Syth in Sethekk Halls. The quest requires heroic versions of both dungeons. These are the terms of a research exchange, not separate historical turning points, and the two halls retain their distinct landscapes in this paired itinerary.

name: Khadgar in Shattrath
description: In Shattrath, Khadgar receives Alturus’s account and sees a familiar problem in it. Karazhan cannot simply be forced open; the Master’s Key once held that power, and he knows the key’s history. He will help restore it, though the next stages will cross Outland’s changed strongholds. The meeting begins the fragment quest line. It is a new undertaking prompted by Alturus’s report, not proof that the Violet Eye has already learned what happened inside the tower.

name: A memory of Arcanagos
description: On the Master’s Terrace, the journal opens onto an older meeting. The blue dragon Arcanagos warns Medivh that a dark power seeks to use him, and urges him to leave the tower. Medivh refuses. Magic burns through the dragon from within; Arcanagos flies away aflame. The scene is a memory carried by the journal, not a new event occurring during the Violet Eye’s present investigation.

name: Nightbane on the terrace
description: With Kalynna’s materials placed in a Blackened Urn, the seeker returns to the Master’s Terrace and sets it alight. The quest says the released energy raises Arcanagos’s charred remains as Nightbane. The adventurer defeats the dragon and carries its essence back to Alturus, whose hope is to study what the fragment may reveal about Medivh. The chain ends with a sample and a research question—not a complete explanation of the Guardian’s magic, nor a later chapter in Arcanagos’s history.

name: Reports from Deadwind Pass
description: Archmage Alturus watches the road below Karazhan while the Violet Eye studies a tower that has kept its doors closed. His first assignments open along two parallel paths: Arcane Disturbances and Restless Activity. One sends the seeker beneath the tower; the other concerns the restless dead around it. The quests establish a troubled place and an order to investigate. They do not establish that either task caused the tower’s condition, or that the source of every disturbance is already known.

name: The key returns to Shattrath
description: The restored key returns to Khadgar in Shattrath, and the attunement chain reaches its stated end. A way into Karazhan now exists. The tower’s condition and the fate of its trapped investigators remain matters for the Violet Eye to examine. That distinction closes one quest and leaves another question standing at the gate.

name: A fragment under the Steamvault
description: The second container is found in the Steamvault beneath Coilfang Reservoir. Khadgar recalls hiding it under Serpent Lake before the place was known by that name; he suspects the naga’s great drain carried it into the reservoir. That explanation is his best account of a changed landscape, not a witnessed transfer. The fragment is recovered, while the precise course of its movement remains uncertain.

name: A separate search for the journal
description: The Violet Eye’s next inquiry is related by the tower, not by a shared quest dependency: after establishing a foothold inside Karazhan and earning the required standing, Alturus asks the adventurer to find Medivh’s Journal. Agents sent before have not returned; Wravien was the last named seeker. This is a distinct research chain joined here for its evidence about the tower’s history. It does not follow automatically from handing Khadgar the key.

name: The investigators among the books
description: Inside the Guardian’s Library, Wravien struggles to remember his commission and sends the seeker to Gradav. Gradav also cannot leave his own work, then points toward Kamsis. The three exchanges make the library’s abundance part of the obstacle: each agent offers a fragment of direction, while none can simply lead the search to its end. Their quest dialogue records confusion and fixation; it does not fully explain what the tower has done to them.

name: The Master’s Touch
description: Khadgar restores the key but says it will remain useless without Medivh’s consent. In the Black Morass, the seeker travels to a remembered past at the Opening of the Dark Portal. There, Medivh recognizes the key as Khadgar’s and acknowledges that he has not yet given it to his apprentice. The meeting belongs to a time-travel quest scene, not to a present-day journey through the swamp. The key receives the permission Khadgar could not grant for himself.

name: The Shade of Aran and the journal
description: Kamsis directs the search toward the Shade of Aran, Medivh’s father. When the shade is overcome, Medivh’s Journal is recovered from the encounter and returned to the Violet Eye’s inquiry. The discovery changes the work from searching for a lost book to reading what the book can reveal. Its pages are not a neutral report from an observer: the next quest treats them as a way to witness one of Medivh’s own memories.

name: The prison above Netherstorm
description: The third fragment lies within the Arcatraz, a prison in the Tempest Keep complex. Khadgar had hidden it while the naaru held the fortress; by the time the seeker arrives, Kael’thas’s forces have turned the vessel into a place of confinement. The key’s last piece is retrieved from a refuge that has become dangerous. The three fragments can now be taken back to their maker.

name: The Dimensius Crisis on K’aresh
description: The struggle over the Dark Heart reaches shattered K’aresh, where the Shadow Guard seeks to restore Dimensius.

name: Kil'jaeden Finds the Draenei on Draenor
description: Kil'jaeden discovered Velen's exiles on Draenor and chose the orc clans as the instrument of his revenge.

name: The Burning Legion Enters Azeroth
description: Demonic forces poured through the portal at Zin-Azshari and began destroying the empire whose court had admitted them.

name: Lei Shen Unites the Mogu
description: Lei Shen overcame rival mogu kings and gathered their competing realms into a single imperial power.

name: The Lich King Falls at Icecrown
description: The campaign through Northrend reached Icecrown, where Arthas's reign as the Lich King ended.

name: The Long Vigil Begins
description: Post-Sundering kaldorei society took up a long watch over Kalimdor and against the return of the Burning Legion.

name: Lordaeron Falls to the Scourge
description: Arthas returned as a death knight, killed his father, and helped bring the kingdom of Lordaeron under the Scourge.

name: Anduin Lothar Falls Near Blackrock Spire
description: Lothar died during the confrontation near Blackrock Spire, creating a moment of shock that Turalyon turned into resolve.

name: The Void Assault on Quel’Thalas
description: Xal’atath and the Devouring Host assault the Sunwell; Quel’Thalas survives the first incursion after defenders force a temporary retreat.

name: The Mogu Empire Expands
description: The new empire subdued neighboring peoples and imposed its rule across much of the southern lands later known as Pandaria.

name: Neltharion Turns the Dragon Soul on His Allies
description: After using the Dragon Soul against the Legion, Neltharion revealed his betrayal and shattered the unity of the dragonflights.

name: Ner'zhul Is Deceived Against the Draenei
description: Kil'jaeden exploited Ner'zhul's authority and grief to turn orc suspicion and violence toward the draenei.

name: The New Horde Crosses to Kalimdor
description: Warned of the coming danger, Thrall led the New Horde west across the sea and began building a future in Kalimdor.

name: Resistance Forms Against the Invasion
description: Kaldorei who rejected Azshara's course organized a resistance in which Malfurion, Tyrande, and Illidan each played consequential roles.

name: Nordrassil Is Planted
description: A World Tree was planted over the new Well at Hyjal, binding the postwar refuge to a new charge of protection.

name: The Assault of N'Zoth Is Defeated
description: Champions carried the struggle into Ny'alotha and ended N'Zoth's immediate assault on Azeroth.

name: N'Zoth Is Unleashed
description: N'Zoth's release brought assaults and corrupting visions against an already wounded Azeroth.

name: Arrival of the Old Gods
description: A group of Old Gods struck Azeroth from the Great Dark, embedded themselves in different parts of the world, and extended their influence toward its core.

name: The Old Gods Are Contained
description: Unable to remove the remaining Old Gods without repeating the wound caused by Y'Shaarj's destruction, the keepers bound them in prisons beneath Azeroth.

name: Scattering of the Old Gods
description: The Void Lords made the Old Gods and cast them through the Great Dark, hoping that some would find and corrupt a world-soul.

name: Blood and the Drakefire Amulet
description: In Upper Blackrock Spire, the adventurers face General Drakkisath and bring his blood to Haleh. From that trial comes the Drakefire Amulet, a ward that allows its bearer to withstand Onyxia’s lair. The Alliance has gone from suspicion to exposure and now to preparation. The key is won; the descent into the dragon’s den waits ahead.

name: A final skull over the Wetlands
description: Axtroz waits amid the windswept Wetlands, where rain and low cloud soften the coast. This final dragon trial completes the tribute demanded by Emberstrife. Across Kalimdor’s distant shores and the Eastern Kingdoms, each challenge has brought the adventurers nearer to the mountain. Now their road turns back to Blackrock, where Drakkisath waits.

name: Finding Rexxar
description: Across Desolace, the adventurers seek Rexxar, a wandering champion of the Horde. His place between the wilds and settled life makes him the guide to a difficult next task. Here the great campaign narrows to a search for one champion moving through an immense, sparse land. Rexxar sets the terms for learning how an adventurer might pass the protections around Onyxia’s lair.

name: A shadow over the Burning Steppes
description: In the Burning Steppes, black dragonkin gather beneath a sky troubled by ash. Their attacks turn a frontier alarm into a question about the reach of the black dragonflight. The Alliance investigation begins with scattered signs and grows toward the mountain that shelters them. The evidence points to a danger with a foothold beyond the wilds; it does not yet reveal the hand guiding Stormwind’s court.

name: A path to Haleh
description: From the capital, the road winds into blue-white winter and brings the adventurers to Haleh. The Dragon’s Eye is the token that opens her counsel, turning Stormwind’s revelation into preparation. She names the test that lies ahead: the blood of a mighty black dragon, taken high within Blackrock Spire. Frost will soon give way to furnace heat.

name: The elder’s counsel
description: At Orgrimmar, Eitrigg’s counsel turns the reports into a charge for the Horde. The old veteran understands the danger gathering around Blackrock and sends the adventurers back toward the stronghold with a clearer purpose. The city’s red stone and timber frame a different kind of authority from Stormwind’s court: experience offered in service to the Horde. Its path leads next to a contest for Blackrock Spire.

name: The dragon who tests the mask
description: In the heat and dark water of Dustwallow Marsh, Emberstrife tests the forged appearance and sends the adventurers to claim dragon skulls from distant guardians. Three trials await beneath different skies, where the black dragonflight and its rivals still shape the wilds. Emberstrife will accept each skull as part of his demand; Myranda’s borrowed shape must hold until the passage is won.

name: A challenge in Blackrock Spire
description: The Horde’s orders bring the adventurers against Warchief Rend Blackhand in Blackrock Spire. His defeat and the proof carried away from it fulfill the charge entrusted to them. The mountain holds more than one danger, and the struggle with Rend belongs to the Horde’s own contest of power. It is a separate road from Windsor’s rescue, even as both paths approach the black dragon’s shadow.

name: The Great Masquerade
description: Before the assembled court, Katrana Prestor’s disguise falls away. The woman who had stood near Stormwind’s seat of power is revealed as Onyxia, the black dragon whose agents troubled the frontier. Dragonkin answer her presence, and Bolvar stands against the assault as the adventurers fight to defend the Keep. The conspiracy is exposed, yet Onyxia escapes the city. Stormwind has found its hidden enemy, not ended the danger.

name: The blood of Drakkisath
description: The Horde returns to Upper Blackrock Spire to confront General Drakkisath. The blood taken from this powerful black dragon completes the trial Rexxar laid before them. The Alliance has passed through its own hands to reach Haleh; the Horde has followed its leaders and its own road. Their stories share a threshold, but each company bears a separate history.

name: The way out of the mountain
description: The escape from Blackrock Depths is hard won. Windsor leads the way through hostile halls while his rescuers hold open each turn in the passage. Stormwind cannot hear its witness while he remains beneath the mountain. When the group emerges, the marshal can return to the city and place what he knows before the people who must judge it.

name: Into the dragon’s lair
description: The Drakefire Amulet opens the way to Onyxia’s Lair, where a band of champions at last faces the black dragon herself. The road began differently for those who came from Stormwind and those who answered the Horde’s call; each company enters beneath its own banners. Fire shivers across the stone as Onyxia takes wing. The struggle reaches its summit in this original Classic account, though its nameless adventurers are remembered as a company, not a single chosen champion.

name: Rexxar’s Drakefire Amulet
description: Back with Rexxar, the adventurers receive the Drakefire Amulet. The token bears the protection gathered from every trial and opens the way before them. The Horde has come to this gate by a road all its own: through intelligence, Eitrigg’s counsel, Thrall’s word, Rexxar’s charge and a dragon’s blood. At the mountain’s foot, that labor gives way to a final descent.

name: A shred of evidence
description: A crumpled note points toward the fragments Windsor needs. The search passes through the forge and deeper chambers of Blackrock Mountain, where small pieces of a document matter more than the strength of the gates. Recovered evidence gives Windsor grounds to leave his cell and face the city again. This is the work of a rescue and an investigation together: one carries the other back into the light.

name: The marshal returns
description: Windsor comes back to Stormwind with the evidence gathered in Blackrock. The capital that once seemed distant from the frontier danger now becomes the stage for its reckoning. Bolvar receives the marshal’s return, and the city’s uneasy court gathers around the claim. The journey has changed the question: instead of asking whether the marshal can escape, the Alliance must decide whether it can hear him.

name: Myranda’s borrowed shape
description: Rexxar’s instruction leads to Myranda the Hag in the blighted Western Plaguelands. Her magic prepares a means of taking a dragon’s shape, a disguise needed for the work to come. It does not make the adventurers dragons or erase their purpose; it is a temporary tool for passing the watchers of the mountain. In the scarred land, the Horde’s road turns from finding an ally to testing a dangerous deception.

name: Three trials, three horizons
description: Three guardians stand in lands far apart: Chronalis beneath the Tanaris sun, Scryer amid Winterspring snow, and Somnus beneath the Swamp of Sorrows’ green canopy. Each place holds its own weather and color, and each dragon bears one part of the trial Emberstrife set. With the three skulls gathered, the Horde can complete his charge and carry Myranda’s borrowed shape toward the black dragon’s mountain.

name: The court’s new voice
description: Reports from Redridge and the Burning Steppes carry the search into Stormwind. In the Keep, Bolvar Fordragon bears the kingdom’s regency while Countess Katrana Prestor speaks with unusual influence. To the investigators, the mystery is no longer only a nest of dragonkin: a trusted figure sits within the very hall they are trying to protect. The resemblance between rumor and conspiracy remains a question still to be proved.

name: Orders from the Badlands
description: Far from Stormwind’s court, the Horde receives a separate summons in the Badlands. Orders point toward the stronghold of Blackrock Spire and the power held there. This path does not begin as an answer to Windsor’s investigation; it grows from Horde intelligence, leaders and obligations of its own. The same mountain appears on another horizon, where a different people must decide what its threat means.

name: Thrall’s account
description: At Orgrimmar, Thrall speaks of the danger and sends the search outward toward Rexxar. The Warchief’s words widen the matter into a concern for the Horde itself. The tale now leaves the city’s red stone and timber for the open country. Ahead lies a champion whose life at the edge of society has made him known across Kalimdor.

name: The marshal in Blackrock Depths
description: Deep in Blackrock Depths, Marshal Windsor has been held away from the court whose danger he understands. His account is not enough by itself to undo the power that silenced him. The adventurers find a soldier who has carried the truth through imprisonment, and a trail of evidence scattered through the fortress. The mountain’s iron rooms have become the place where a political mystery waits for its missing proof.

name: Orc Clans Drink Mannoroth's Blood
description: Many orc leaders accepted Mannoroth's blood and its power, binding the Horde more deeply to the Legion; Durotan kept the Frostwolves from drinking.

name: Orgrim Doomhammer Becomes Warchief
description: Orgrim killed Blackhand, broke much of the Shadow Council's concealed power, and assumed leadership of the Horde.

name: The Dark Portal Leads Back to Outland
description: A renewed passage through the Dark Portal carried Azeroth's forces into shattered Outland and the conflicts rooted there.

name: The Pandaren Revolution
description: Resistance associated with Kang spread among the mogu's subject peoples until the imperial order broke and the southern lands entered a new age.

name: Pandaria Returns to the Wider World
description: The long-hidden land of Pandaria became a theater of exploration and intensifying Alliance–Horde conflict.

name: The Pantheon Departs
description: With Azeroth stabilized and its guardians appointed, the Pantheon departed while the keepers and titan-forged remained to watch over the world.

name: The Pantheon Discovers Azeroth
description: Aggramar discovered Azeroth's nascent titan and the Old Gods rooted around it, bringing the imperiled world to the Pantheon's attention.

name: Gathering of the Pantheon
description: The awakened titans found one another, formed the Pantheon, and traveled onward to order worlds and seek more of their kind.

name: Emergence of the Physical Universe
description: The conflict between primordial Light and Void gave rise to the physical universe, while released energies formed the Twisting Nether.

name: The Plague Spreads Through Lordaeron
description: A mysterious plague spread through Lordaeron as the Cult of the Damned and Scourge prepared the kingdom's destruction.

name: The Portal at the Well Collapses
description: The defenders disrupted the Legion's gateway before Sargeras could enter, and the unstable Well collapsed around the broken portal.

name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Are Founded
description: The exiles established Quel'Thalas in the northern Eastern Kingdoms and created the Sunwell as the heart of their new civilization.

name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Fall
description: The Scourge broke Quel'Thalas, raised Sylvanas into undeath, and corrupted the Sunwell while advancing its larger design.

name: Quel'Thalas and Arathor Form a Wartime Alliance
description: Facing an overwhelming Amani assault, Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor and shared limited arcane instruction in exchange for military aid.

name: Ragnaros Re-emerges at Blackrock
description: A desperate Dark Iron summoning brought Ragnaros back into the world, devastated the southern mountains, and ended the dwarven war beneath a new volcanic power.

name: The key and the armies
description: The three recovered fragments returned to the bronze dragon, and the scepter could be made whole. Beyond that personal journey, Horde and Alliance communities were gathering the supplies for a campaign in Silithus. The key alone was not the war effort. Workshops, stores and countless contributions prepared the force that would have to stand before the opened stronghold. Rival peoples worked toward the same threshold, without losing the histories that divided them. The coming battle required both the recovered artifact and the many hands that no single quest could name.

name: Blue shard — A dragon who wished to be left alone
description: On Azshara's coast, Azuregos offered a very different account of guardianship. The shard had drawn attention he did not want, interrupting his study of the ancient shore. He had hidden it with an enchanted fish, making an ordinary search of the sea hopeless. His solution for its recovery was an arcanite buoy that would draw the creature out. The instructions lay in a ledger, and the ledger had to be taken to Narain Soothfancy in Tanaris. The blue trail began with a dragon's evasion and became an engineer's problem.

name: Beyond the wall, beneath the temple
description: The campaign continued into the Ruins and the Temple of Ahn'Qiraj. Beyond the qiraji armies lay C'Thun, the deeper threat against which the preparations had been gathered. Victory there gave the opened gate its purpose: the company had not restored a key merely to release what waited behind the wall. It had restored a way to reach that danger. The victory brought this campaign to its close, after a long road from the bronze dragon’s vigil. The scepter's legacy joins the losses of the first war to the collective labor of the second.

name: Red shard — Beyond the dragon’s suffering
description: The red trail ended with Nefarian's defeat and the recovery of the fragment before it could be destroyed. When it was brought back to Anachronos, the bronze dragon spoke of Vaelastrasz's soul finding rest. The shard was not merely a treasure won from a raid. Its return fulfilled the charge of a guardian whose own strength had failed him. One piece of the scepter was recovered, but the cost of its keeping remained part of the story that the restored artifact would carry.

name: Blue shard — The chef and the Isle of Dread
description: Another of Narain's demands led to Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan. The chef's answer sent the adventurers out to the Isle of Dread, off Feralas, to hunt the chimaerok and secure the ingredients for his formidable meal. The scale of the task belonged to the same curious bargain as the goggles: the world's key depended upon satisfying the engineer's requirements. This branch brought the search from desert workshops to a dangerous island, where even preparing a feast called for allies rather than a solitary traveler.

name: Blue shard — Libraries, demons, and dragon lairs
description: The missing chapters drew the adventurers through places that rarely belonged to one journey. Pages awaited in Stormwind and Undercity, in the dangerous reaches of Winterspring and the Blasted Lands, and on Doctor Weavil's Alcaz Island. Others required the company to return to Blackwing Lair, confront Onyxia, and reach Ragnaros in Molten Core. A single scattered volume bound these distant dangers to the same unfinished work. The reconstructed volume gave Narain the means to continue the work Azuregos had set before him.

name: Green shard — The guardian returns
description: Tyrande's arrival brought the intervention the defenders had awaited. Eranikus was redeemed, and Remulos spoke of his return to the Dream to confront the wrong he had done. The green fragment could now be carried back to Anachronos. Unlike the red trail, this recovery left its guardian able to return to his own work. The two journeys shared a broken scepter, but their endings were different: one honored a lost watcher; the other restored a watcher to the struggle from which he had fallen.

name: Green shard — The gathering of corruption
description: Remulos's preparations sent the adventurers to the forest portals associated with the Dream. The search ranged through Duskwood, Ashenvale, Feralas and the Hinterlands, gathering the fragments needed for the next confrontation. These were separate places bound by one danger, rather than a single road across the forest. The journey widened the threat beyond the temple where it had begun. By returning with the corruption's traces, the seekers made possible the attempt to draw Eranikus into Moonglade, where his redemption could be sought.

name: Green shard — A guardian lost to the Nightmare
description: The green trail began beneath the marshes, in the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. Near the Shade of Eranikus, Malfurion's appearance directed the search beyond the temple and toward his agent in Teldrassil. From the forest wisp, the road led to Keeper Remulos in Moonglade. The green shard could not be reclaimed by treating its guardian as another enemy to be slain. The search had reached a dragon ensnared by the Nightmare, and the help it sought would have to reach him through that corruption.

name: The memory at the Scarab Wall
description: Before seeking the scattered pieces, the adventurers returned to the place where the bond had broken. At the Scarab Wall, the old struggle was shown again: dragons pressing back the qiraji, defenders reaching the barrier, and Fandral turning away from the offered key. This was no new battle in Silithus. It was the past made visible to those who would inherit its unfinished task. The scepter could open a gate; the memory explained why that gate had first been closed, and why its key had been rejected.

name: Blue shard — From Silverpine to Molten Core
description: Narain could not turn the ledger into a finished answer without further help. His missing scrying goggles led the seekers to Stewvul, his former friend, hiding in a crate near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine. Stewvul no longer had them: the search continued into Molten Core. Thus a quarrel between gnomes carried the greater quest beneath Blackrock Mountain. The equipment had to be recovered before Narain's work could proceed, binding an apparently small personal errand to the fate of the unopened gates.

name: Blue shard — The beast in the Bay of Storms
description: With the preparations complete, the blue trail returned to the sea. Narain sent the adventurers to the Bay of Storms in Azshara with the arcanite buoy, warning them of Maws. The creature that held the shard could be drawn from hiding, but recovering it demanded companions ready for the danger that answered. When the blue fragment was won, the instructions were at last simple: carry it to Anachronos. An old dragon's elaborate concealment had become a journey through much of Azeroth before ending on its storm-bound coast.

name: Green shard — Restraint at Nighthaven
description: When Eranikus entered Nighthaven, the duty was to endure him, not to kill him. Keeper Remulos had to survive, and the settlement had to be defended while Tyrande approached. The dragon's assault and the shades of the Nightmare made that restraint costly. Yet destroying him would defeat the purpose for which the defenders had gathered. Their task was to hold the space in which rescue remained possible: to stand against his violence without surrendering the hope that the guardian beneath it could be freed.

name: Blue shard — A ransom in the snow
description: The search for Narain's book brought back a ransom letter instead of the missing volume. Its captors demanded payment, and Narain answered with a deception of his own. He gave the adventurers clothing to take his place and a sack of rocks to stand for gold. The appointed meeting lay in Winterspring, far from his desert home. There the false payment brought the seekers into the encounter with Number Two. The scheme did not recover the book; its pages still had to be gathered by another road.

name: Flashback · Era 5 — A victory without comfort
description: At the gate, Merithra, Arygos and Caelestrasz held the enemy back while Anachronos and the defenders raised the barrier. When the seal was made, the bronze dragon offered Fandral a scepter and a gong: a means to open the way if the need returned. Fandral would accept no further burden from that victory. His son was gone; the stronghold still stood. He cast the scepter against the barrier and shattered it. Anachronos gathered the fragments, preserving a duty that grief had refused.

name: The road from Cenarion Hold
description: The later journey began in Silithus, where Baristolth of the Shifting Sands directed seekers toward the bronze dragon at the Caverns of Time. Anachronos did not simply place the world's burden in the first hands that reached him. The path demanded evidence of resolve. It led into Blackwing Lair, to Broodlord Lashlayer, before the deeper work of gaining the brood's trust. The task was already larger than one traveler: a champion's progress depended upon companions willing to enter the mountain together.

name: Flashback · Era 5 — The war that raised the wall
description: Long before the adventurers came to Silithus, the night elves had fought a war beneath its harsh southern sky. Fandral Staghelm led their defense against the qiraji, and his son Valstann fell in the struggle. The dragonflights joined the battle, but neither courage nor ancient power could make the loss undone. As the defenders were driven toward Ahn'Qiraj, the question before them became how to contain an enemy they could not wholly destroy. The wall that later generations would find was born of that necessity.

name: The gates open
description: When the preparations had brought the campaign to the Scarab Wall, the restored scepter could be raised against the gong. The barrier made by the ancient defenders opened, and the danger it had contained came forth. The ensuing struggle was remembered as the Ten-Hour War. The relic's recovery had not ended the conflict; it had made the confrontation possible. Where Fandral once turned away from the gate in grief, a later generation now stood together before the consequences of opening it.

name: Red shard — The captive guardian
description: In Blackwing Lair, Vaelastrasz could no longer fulfill his charge by surrendering the red shard. Nefarian held it, and threatened to destroy it. The wounded red dragon's appeal made the recovery urgent: the loss of that fragment would deny the seekers their key to Ahn'Qiraj. Here the search for an ancient relic entered a living act of cruelty. The adventurers had to carry Vaelastrasz's last request through the fortress of the very enemy who had brought him low.

name: The keepers of a broken promise
description: The broken scepter did not pass out of history. Its pieces remained in the keeping of dragons, yet the long vigil brought troubles of its own. When Anachronos later named Eranikus, Vaelastrasz and Azuregos, his warning carried the weight of disappointed trust. Each guardian's story had turned toward tragedy or estrangement. To restore the key, mortal seekers would have to enter those stories. A thousand years separated the wars, but time had not protected the watchers from the wounds of the world.

name: The journey that outlived the gong
description: The gong belonged to a brief opening in the campaign, but the quest's final recognition was not identical to that moment. Treasure of the Timeless One remained a distinct conclusion for those who held the restored scepter after the opening war. Remembering that distinction keeps the journey larger than a race for a title. Across forests, libraries, mountains and seas, the work had gathered companions around a broken promise. Its completion remembered the long recovery, as well as the threshold that recovery had allowed the world to cross.

name: Blue shard — A book scattered to the winds
description: Narain's missing volume of Draconic for Dummies became another obstacle. Doctor Weavil had intervened, and the book was torn into eight chapters. Narain supplied a magical binding, but the scattered pages had to be found before the volume could be made whole. The search now reached far beyond Tanaris. A text needed to understand the ledger became a second broken object within the greater quest: before the dragon's key could be restored, the engineer's book had to be restored as well.

name: The Second War Begins
description: The Horde drove north while the newly formed Alliance organized a defense across several kingdoms and theaters.

name: The Covenant Campaigns Converge
description: Champions worked among distinct covenant realms whose campaigns formed the broad framework of resistance in the afterlife.

name: Shattrath Falls to the Horde
description: The Horde's assault devastated Shattrath and broke the principal center of organized draenei resistance, though draenei survivors endured.

name: The Siege Ends Garrosh's Rule
description: Opposition from within and beyond the Horde converged on Orgrimmar and ended Garrosh Hellscream's rule.

name: The Primordial Imbalance
description: As Azeroth's world-soul developed, it consumed much of the fifth element, Spirit, leaving the native elementals without its balancing influence.

name: Stormwind Falls
description: The Horde captured and devastated Stormwind, forcing surviving leaders and refugees to flee north.

name: Stratholme Is Purged
description: Convinced Stratholme's people were infected, Arthas ordered the city purged; Jaina and Uther rejected the course, deepening his isolation.

name: The Sunwell Becomes the Darkwell
description: Xal’atath channels Void power into the Sunwell, transforming it into the Darkwell as Alleria and Turalyon vanish into its depths.

name: Survivors Reach Mount Hyjal
description: Many surviving defenders reached the lands around Mount Hyjal, carrying the memory of the lost world into the beginning of the Long Vigil.

name: Thoradin Unites Arathor
description: Thoradin brought scattered human tribes beneath one banner and established Arathor around the fortified center of Strom.

name: Thrall Liberates Interned Orcs
description: Thrall freed orcs from internment and gathered a new Horde whose purpose was not identical to the conquered Old Horde.

name: The Titan-forged Are Mustered
description: The Pantheon created armies of stone and metal and empowered the greatest among them as keepers to lead the war for Azeroth.

name: Turalyon Rallies the Alliance
description: Turalyon rallied the shaken Alliance and sustained the counteroffensive that drove the Horde south.

name: The Veil into the Shadowlands Is Shattered
description: Sylvanas shattered the veil between life and death, drawing champions into the Shadowlands and its covenant realms.

name: The War Within Opens in Khaz Algar
description: Xal'atath's gathering threat led champions into Khaz Algar and its subterranean worlds, where the Earthen became central allies and witnesses.

name: The World-wound Is Stabilized
description: The keepers raised wards around Azeroth's bleeding wound until its arcane energies settled into the Well of Eternity.

name: Ancient Allies Join the Defense
description: Cenarius and other powers of ancient Kalimdor joined the defense, while the Dragon Aspects prepared a weapon intended to drive back the Legion.

name: The World-forges Are Established
description: The keepers established complementary facilities in the far north and south to stabilize Azeroth and sustain the work of ordering it.

name: The Removal of Y'Shaarj
description: Aman’Thul tore Y'Shaarj from Azeroth, destroying the Old God but opening a terrible wound in the sleeping world-soul.

name: The Battle of Mount Hyjal
description: A temporary coalition delayed Archimonde's advance long enough for Malfurion to call upon Nordrassil's power and destroy him.

name: The Elemental Assault on the Black Empire
description: For the first time, Azeroth's rival elemental hosts united against the Old Gods and attacked the Black Empire's growing cities.

name: The Elemental Wars
description: The four Elemental Lords and their hosts fought across primordial Azeroth for ages, with dominion shifting continually and no lasting victor.

name: The First War
description: A multi-year invasion in which the Old Horde crossed from Draenor, fought the Kingdom of Stormwind, changed leadership, and ultimately captured the southern capital.

name: The Fourth War Campaign
description: A strategic dossier of the faction war's widening fronts, internal rebellion, and political conclusion.

name: The Frozen Throne Campaign
description: A cross-world sequence in which Illidan established power in Outland, returned to strike Icecrown, and lost the final race to Arthas.

name: The Icecrown Citadel Campaign
description: A broad strategic dossier tracing the coalition's advance through Icecrown to the fall of Arthas as the Lich King.

name: The Second War
description: A multi-theater war in which the Horde drove north against the Alliance of Lordaeron before internal fracture and an Alliance counteroffensive reversed the campaign.

name: The Titan-forged War against the Black Empire
description: Keeper-led armies of stone and metal fought across primordial Azeroth, defeated the Black Empire's forces, and subdued the powers that had ruled the world.

name: The Troll–Aqir War
description: A long, multi-front struggle in which the Empire of Zul resisted the aqir and pursued their retreating forces toward the distant reaches of Kalimdor.

name: The Troll Wars
description: A multi-stage war in which the Amani offensive against Quel'Thalas drew the high elves and Arathor into a decisive alliance.

name: The Visions of N'Zoth Campaign
description: A strategic dossier of N'Zoth's assaults, the defense of mind and world, and the campaign into Ny'alotha.

name: The War Against the Burning Legion
description: A cross-world strategic dossier from the Legion's return to the coalition's campaign on Argus.

name: The War of the Ancients
description: A continent-spanning war in which the Burning Legion devastated ancient Kalimdor before a changing alliance disrupted the gateway at the Well.

name: The War of the Three Hammers
description: A dwarven succession war drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from Ironforge, opened new centers, and ended when Ragnaros's return devastated the southern mountains.

name: Campaigns of the Adventuring Age
description: A dossier index for the Northrend war and the later world-to-world campaign against the Burning Legion.

name: Ancient Kalimdor Conflicts
description: A research grouping for the long wars that redistributed peoples and power before kaldorei ascendance, beginning with the supported troll–aqir campaign.

name: The Elemental Resistance to the Black Empire
description: A descriptive campaign grouping for the Elemental Lords' united attempt to remove the Old Gods and their growing empire.

name: The Elemental Wars
description: A descriptive campaign grouping for the prolonged struggle among Azeroth's four elemental hosts.

name: Wars of a Wounded World
description: A dossier index for the Fourth War and the assaults surrounding N'Zoth's release.

name: Conflicts of the Post-Sundering Kingdoms
description: An atlas-scale grouping for the two best-supported conflicts that materially redistributed power during Era 5: the Troll Wars and the War of the Three Hammers.

name: The Rise of the Horde and the First Two Wars
description: A cross-world strategic grouping from the Horde's formation and draenei war through the First and Second Wars, ending with the Old Horde's defeat and destruction of the original Dark Portal.

name: The Third War and the Frozen Throne
description: A strategic grouping of the coalition defense at Mount Hyjal and the later cross-world contest that ended at the Frozen Throne.

name: The Titan-forged War for Azeroth
description: An editorial campaign grouping for the keeper-led war that broke the Black Empire and made containment and planetary repair possible.

name: The War of the Ancients Campaign
description: A strategic grouping of the Legion invasion, the widening defense of Kalimdor, the betrayal of Neltharion, and the final convergence at the Well.

name: Arator's Relics of Light
description: Arator searches for Light relics while confronting family, faith, and the defense of Quel'Thalas during Midnight.

name: Beyond the Dark Portal
description: After the Second War, the Alliance crosses into Draenor while Ner'zhul's portal ritual tears the world toward Outland.

name: Oronok and the Cipher of Damnation
description: Oronok Torn-heart and his sons recover the Cipher's fragments across Shadowmoon Valley before a final confrontation.

name: Darrowshire: Lost and Remembered
description: Pamela Redpath's quest revisits a village destroyed by the Scourge and the Battle of Darrowshire.

name: The Defias Across Two Generations
description: The Defias Brotherhood's grievance, Edwin VanCleef's rebellion, and Vanessa's later vengeance form a generational history of Westfall and Stormwind.

name: Dragonwrath and the Blue Flight
description: Malygos's death leaves the Blue Dragonflight divided as Anachronos's warning draws mortals into the Dragonwrath quest.

name: The Heartsbane of Drustvar
description: Ancient Drust hostility and the Waycrests' private grief converge in a witchcraft crisis across Drustvar.

name: The Veiled Blade and Lord Valthalak
description: Anthion seeks the rescue of Ysida from Stratholme; afterward, the Veiled Blade’s divided amulet draws an adventurer through its scattered companions to Valthalak’s old lair.

name: The Fallen Hero and Rakh’likh
description: Two faction paths lead to Trebor, whose return to the Blasted Lands is bound to his captured soldiers. Their spirits are freed, and the search for a demon’s true name and a Felbane weapon leads to Razelikh.

name: Fangs of the Father
description: Wrathion's origins and covert campaign against corrupted black dragons unfold through the rogue legendary quest.

name: Galakrond and the Five Proto-Dragons
description: Galakrond's predation draws Tyr and five proto-dragons into a struggle that precedes the dragonflights' rise.

name: Gilneas: Exile and Return
description: The worgen curse, Forsaken invasion, years of exile, and later reclamation form a long story of home and identity.

name: Karazhan: The Master’s Key and Nightbane
description: Alturus’s investigation leads Khadgar to restore a key divided across Outland. A separate Violet Eye search for Medivh’s Journal uncovers a memory of Arcanagos and a ritual that raises Nightbane.

name: Khadgar, Garona, and the Ring
description: On alternate Draenor, Khadgar's legendary-ring campaign intersects with Garona's control and Gul'dan's Shadow Council.

name: From Sunwell to Dawnwell
description: The Void invasion of Quel'Thalas, the Sunwell's transformation into the Darkwell, and the elven coalition's response form an ongoing modern arc.

name: Nazmir, the Loa, and G'huun
description: Talanji's expedition seeks loa allies against blood trolls whose rituals serve G'huun.

name: Quel'Delar Restored
description: A lost blade's hilt leads through identification, reforging, purification, and a contested return at the Sunwell.

name: Saurfang's Rebellion
description: The Fourth War divides the Horde as Saurfang's dissent, Baine's rescue, and rival loyalist paths converge on Orgrimmar.

name: The Scepter of the Shifting Sands
description: A shattered key to Ahn'Qiraj links an ancient night elf and dragonflight war to a later quest, a shared war effort, and the opening of the Scarab Wall.

name: The Dragon in Stormwind
description: A conspiracy reaches from the Burning Steppes into Stormwind’s court while a separate Horde intelligence path follows Rexxar toward Onyxia’s lair.

name: Suramar and the Nightwell
description: Suramar's ancient refuge becomes a modern point of dependence and conflict when the Legion returns and rebellion grows under Elisande's rule.

name: The Thunder King Returns
description: Lei Shen's ancient dominion and later return bring Zandalari forces, pandaren defenders, and both factions to the Isle of Thunder.

name: Vol'dun and Sethraliss
description: Exile, Jakra'zet's secret plans, sethrak divisions, and the endangered Temple of Sethraliss shape the desert's campaign.

name: The War of the Shifting Sands
description: The night elves, qiraji, and dragonflights fight a war that ends with Ahn'Qiraj sealed behind the Scarab Wall.

name: The Wrathgate and Undercity
description: The Wrathgate disaster breaks an offensive against the Lich King and sends Alliance and Horde toward the Battle for Undercity.

name: Wrathion's Legendary Cloak
description: Wrathion's Pandaria trials draw both factions into his search for strength against a wider threat.
